breaks.expected: A key of wrong length should surface as integrity_key_missing/tampered AND be removable through the explicit discard path (discardCorrupt should discard the unusable key, or a dedicated typed recovery exists), so the wallet is not permanently unwritable for every owner. Corrupt state must have a bounded, explicit recovery — never a dead end that also destroys an intact wallet.
breaks.observed: With no wallet stored: every replace throws tampered ('integrity key has unexpected length') and discardCorrupt(owner) returns .notCorrupt; no API sequence recovers (VERIFIED). With an intact wallet stored: load -> tampered, discardCorrupt deletes the (valid) wallet item but leaves the corrupt key, so the next replace is still tampered; owner B (never stored) is also blocked and discardCorrupt(ownerB) reports not_corrupt (VERIFIED). A single corrupt 32-byte device key is device-wide: it takes every account's wallet with it.

breaks.expected: Per the W05 program text ("trusted time and rollback") and the objective's tamper detection, a rollback to an earlier authentic envelope must be detected (e.g. a separately stored high-water revision or the same fence the JS side relies on) and surfaced as a typed failure, not read as current state. NOTE: on Apple this requires Keychain-write access as the app (jailbreak/backup-restore/attacker with device key), so I rate P1 not P0; the judge may downgrade to P2 if anti-rollback is explicitly out of W05-01 scope (the objective lists only 'tamper detection').
breaks.observed: load returns revision 1 with grant G available and receipts [] — no error, no rollback detection (VERIFIED). The envelope has no monotonic-revision / anti-rollback fence outside the item itself.
breaks.repro: `swift test --filter OfflineWalletAttackTests.testAttack03` on the surrogate package (exit 1, 1 executed / 0 passed / 1 failed). Store rev 1 {grant G}, replace to rev 2 {no grants, receipt R (G spent)}, then restore the captured rev-1 bytes into the wallet item; load(owner).

breaks.expected: Limits must be consistent: either the envelope budget covers max grants x max receipts at max payload for realistic JSON, or the per-item/count limits are documented as lower. A validate()-accepted wallet must be storable.
breaks.observed: `capacityExceeded — wallet exceeds 1048576 bytes; only 61 such receipts fit beside 8 maximal grants` (VERIFIED). Control test 04b with quote-free payloads of the same byte size passes, proving the JSON re-escaping of realistic receipts (quotes/backslashes) blows the envelope budget. A device that legitimately accumulates 62-64 unsent receipts while offline cannot persist the next receipt -> a spend whose receipt cannot be stored (offline allocation != consumption invariant at risk, since the grant was consumed but the receipt is unstorable).
breaks.repro: `swift test --filter OfflineWalletAttackTests.testAttack04_` (exit 1, 2 executed / 1 passed / 1 failed). Contents pass OfflineWallet.validate (every item within Limits.maxGrantJwsBytes / maxReceiptPayloadBytes and counts <= maxGrants/maxReceipts) yet replace throws.

breaks.expected: The core should enforce the fence atomically (serialise within OfflineWallet, or re-verify stored revision under a lock before write), or the contract that ALL access must go through PickleOfflineWallet's queue should be enforced/documented in the core (e.g. an actor). Lost unsent receipts violate 'partial/replayed results never consume a credit' auditability.
breaks.observed: A's replace also succeeds at revision 2 and overwrites B's wallet — receipt R2 (an unsent receipt) is silently dropped (VERIFIED). The revision fence is check-then-write with no atomic compare-and-swap or in-core lock; only the RN bridge's serial queue prevents this, so any second core client (Swift-side sync worker, app extension, tests, future native caller) or process-level concurrency defeats it.
breaks.repro: `swift test --filter OfflineWalletAttackTests.testAttack06` (exit 1, 1 executed / 0 passed / 1 failed). Two OfflineWallet instances over one store; instance A's replace(expected=1) is interleaved (during its read) by instance B's replace(expected=1) which commits rev 2 with receipt R2; then A's write commits.
breaks.title: Two OfflineWallet instances (or any use outside the bridge's serial queue) lose updates: interleaved replace succeeds instead of revision_conflict

breaks.expected: readVerified/replace should refuse or cap revisions >= 2^53 as tampered/unsupported, or discardCorrupt should treat 'unreadable from the bridge' as corrupt, so the JS side is never presented with an unrecoverable wallet.
breaks.observed: replace at expected=9007199254740991 succeeds and returns revision 9007199254740992; OfflineWallet.revision(fromBridge: 9007199254740992) throws invalid_revision and the TS parseSnapshot rejects it — the wallet becomes unreachable from JS (every fence fails), yet discardCorrupt returns not_corrupt so it cannot be discarded either (VERIFIED). Practically unreachable by counting (2^53 replaces) — hence P2 — but reachable via any forged/migrated envelope.
breaks.repro: `swift test --filter OfflineWalletAttackTests.testAttack05` (exit 1, 2 executed / 0 passed / 2 failed) plus candidate's own revision(fromBridge:) boundary.

breaks.expected: A typed OfflineWalletError (tampered / unsupported / invalid_revision) — an app crash is never an acceptable outcome of reading persisted state. Fix is one line (`addingReportingOverflow` or refusing revisions >= 2^53 in readVerified).

OfflineWallet.replace(ownerId:expectedRevision:contents:)` (VERIFIED on Linux x86_64 Swift 6.0.3; Swift arithmetic overflow traps identically on arm64 — INFERRED for iOS). Requires a MAC-valid envelope, i.e. same-device key access; not reachable by normal counting, hence P2 rather than P0.

breaks.observed: loadOfflineWallet(OWNER) resolves with a snapshot for OTHER_OWNER (and replace with an upper-cased owner) instead of bridge_contract (VERIFIED). Native does bind owner, so this only matters if the native side is wrong/racing an account switch — defence in depth missing at the JS boundary.

breaks.expected: parseSnapshot rejects duplicate ids / empty ids / over-capacity / non-object payloadJson as bridge_contract.
breaks.observed: A snapshot with two identical grantIds is accepted (first mismatch reported; the loop stops at the first accepted case) (VERIFIED). Same trust-gap class as J1: the typed JS layer is strict on primitives but not on the invariants the native core enforces.

breaks.expected: Only tampered / integrity_key_missing / unsupported_version are valid discard outcomes; anything else is bridge_contract.
